recipes.name: KPop Demon Hunters Airplane Feast
ingredients: 8 oz Korean radish, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick
1 small yellow onion, cut into 1 inch pieces
5 cups all purpose flour, divided (625 g)
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more as needed when cooking
2–3 links Korean blood sausage (sundae), store bought
instructions: For Eomuk Guk (Fish Cake Soup):
For the For the Servings: 3–4
For the Estimated Time: 45 minutes
For the Skewers
Rinse and cook tteokbokki rice cakes according to package directions, then cool and skewer. - 3 skewered tteokbokki
Thread flat and round fish cakes onto skewers in a wavy pattern. - 3 skewered flat fish cakes - 3 skewered round fish cakes
For the Broth

In a Dutch oven, combine water, anchovy-seaweed broth packet, Korean radish (sliced ¼-inch thick), small yellow onion (cut into chunks) - 8 cups water - 1 large anchovy seaweed broth packet - 8 oz Korean radish peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick - 1 small yellow onion cut into 1 inch pieces
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain through a colander, reserving the radish and discarding solids.
Return broth to pot and add:soy sauce, Korean tuna sauce, minced garlic - 1 tbsp soy sauce - ½ tbsp Korean tuna sauce - 1 tbsp minced garlic
Cover and keep warm.
For the Dipping Sauce
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, water, gochugaru, rice vinegar, and chopped scallion. Mix well. - ¼ cup soy sauce - 2 tbsp water - 1 ½ tsp gochugaru - 1 tbsp rice vinegar - 1 scallion chopped
For the Serving
Bring broth to a simmer and add skewers. Cook for about 10 minutes until fish cakes puff.
Add reserved radish during the last 1–2 minutes.
Ladle soup into bowls, top with thinly sliced scallions, and serve with dipping sauce. - 2 scallions thinly sliced, to garnish
For Gimbap:
For the For the Servings: 4–6
For the Estimated Time: 60 minutes
For the Rice
Add short grain rice to a rice cooker bowl and rinse under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. - 2 cups short grain rice
Add water and a pinch of kosher salt, then cook using the sushi rice setting (or cook normally on stovetop). - 2 ¼ cups water - kosher salt
Once cooked, transfer rice to a bowl and drizzle with toasted sesame oil. Mix gently, cover, and keep warm. - toasted sesame oil
For the Egg
Heat vegetable oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. - 1 tsp vegetable oil
Season well-beaten eggs with a pinch of kosher salt, then pour into the pan. Swirl to form a thin, even layer. - 2 well beaten eggs - pinch of kosher salt
Cook gently until set, flip carefully, and finish cooking with residual heat. Transfer to a cutting board and slice into thin strips.
For the Spinach
In the same skillet, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. - ½ tsp vegetable oil
Add minced garlic cloves and a pinch of kosher salt, sautéing for 30 seconds. - 2 minced garlic cloves - pinch of kosher salt
Add spinach and soy sauce, cover, and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Transfer to a bowl. - 8 oz spinach - 1 tsp soy sauce
For the Carrots
In the same skillet, heat another vegetable oil over medium heat. - ½ tsp vegetable oil
Add medium carrot (peeled and julienned) with a pinch of kosher salt, sautéing for 4–5 minutes until slightly softened. Transfer to a bowl. - 1 medium carrot (peeled and julienned) - kosher salt
For the Remaining Fillings
Slice English cucumber into ½-inch thick strips. - 1 English cucumber
Slice yellow pickled radish (danmuji) into matching strips. - 1 yellow pickled radish (danmuji)
Cut imitation crab sticks to match size if needed. - 2 imitation crab sticks
Prepare Korean burdock root strips and slice spam/ham into long strips. - 2 Korean burdock root strips - spam/ham
For the Assembly
Place a sheet of gim (roasted seaweed) on a bamboo rolling mat.
Spread a thin, even layer of warm rice across the seaweed, leaving 1–2 inches at the top edge.
Arrange fillings across the center: cucumber strip, pickled radish strip, burdock root, sautéed carrots, spinach, imitation crab, egg strips, spam/ham
Roll tightly using the bamboo mat, sealing the edge with exposed rice. Gently compress the roll.
Brush the outside lightly with toasted sesame oil, then slice into ½-inch rounds using a sharp knife.
Serve immediately.
For Naengmyeon (Korean cold noodle soup):
Prepare prepackaged Hansang naengmyeon soup and noodles according to package instructions (boil noodles, rinse cold, and chill broth). - prepackaged Hansang Soup
Transfer noodles to a bowl and pour over cold broth.
Top with English cucumber (thinly sliced), pickled radish, 1 hardboiled egg (halved) - ¼ English cucumber sliced - pickled radish - 1 egg hardboiled
Serve immediately, ice-cold.
For Hotteok (Korean sweet pancake):
For the Servings: 16 pancakes
For the Estimated Time: 2 hours
For the Dough

In a large mixing bowl, combine lukewarm water, white sugar, instant yeast, kosher salt, and vegetable oil. Whisk gently. - ¼ cup white sugar - 4 tsp instant yeast - 1 tsp kosher salt - 2 tbsp vegetable oil plus more as needed when cooking
Add all-purpose flour, mixing until a sticky dough forms. - 5 cups all purpose flour divided (625 g)
Cover with greased plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place for 60–90 minutes, until doubled.
For the Filling
In a bowl, mix dark brown sugar, chopped walnuts, cinnamon, and kosher salt. Set aside. - 1 cup dark brown sugar - ¼ cup chopped walnuts - 1 ½ tsp cinnamon - ½ tsp kosher salt
For the Shaping
Punch down the risen dough and let it rest for 10–20 minutes.
Turn onto a floured surface using about additional flour. - all purpose flour divided (625 g)
Divide into 16 pieces. Flatten each into a 4-inch disk, add 1–2 tablespoons filling, and seal into a ball.
For the Cooking
Heat vegetable oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. - vegetable oil plus more as needed when cooking
Place dough balls in the pan and cook for 30 seconds until lightly golden. Flip and press into a 6-inch pancake.
Cook 1–2 minutes per side until golden brown, reducing heat to low and covering briefly to finish cooking through.
Repeat and serve warm.
Optional but highly recommended: draw little cat faces on top with edible markers, because that’s part of the aesthetic.
For Sundae (Blood Sausage):
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat and add neutral oil. - 1 tablespoon neutral oil
Slice the Korean blood sausage links into thick, bite-sized rounds.

Add the sliced blood sausage to the pan in a single layer. Sauté for 4–6 minutes, flipping occasionally, until heated through and lightly crisped on the outside. - 2–3 links Korean blood sausage (sundae) store bought
Cook until the exterior develops some color but the interior stays soft and bouncy.
Transfer to a plate and serve hot alongside the rest of the feast.
